def-connected-poincare-cover-and-positiv:
## Definition

Fix an integer spacetime dimension $D\ge2$ and the mostly-plus form
$$
\eta(p,a)=-p^0a^0+\sum_{j=1}^{D-1}p^ja^j.
$$
Let $e_0=(1,0,\ldots,0)$, and let
$$
L=SO_0(D-1,1)=\{\Lambda\in GL_D(\mathbb R):\Lambda^T\eta\Lambda=\eta,\ \det\Lambda=1,\ \Lambda e_0\text{ is future-pointing}\}
$$
be the proper orthochronous Lorentz group, the identity component of the indicated matrix group. A **connected Lorentz cover** is a connected Lie group $K$ with a covering homomorphism $c:K\to L$ in the sense of [[def-covering-homomorphism-of-lie-groups]]. It acts on translations $N=(\mathbb R^D,+)$ by $\alpha_k(a)=c(k)a$. The associated connected-cover Poincaré group is the external semidirect product
$G=\mathbb R^D\rtimes_\alpha K,\qquad (a,k)(b,\ell)=(a+c(k)b,k\ell).$
with its product topology, using [[def-external-semidirect-product]] and [[thm-external-semidirect-product-is-a-group]].

For $p\in\mathbb R^D$, write
$$
\chi_p(a)=\exp(i\eta(p,a))\in\mathbb T.
$$
This is a continuous character of $(\mathbb R^D,+)$; the Pontryagin dual and its compact-open topology are those of [[def-pontryagin-dual-and-compact-open-topology]]. Put $\widehat C_+=\{\chi_p:p^0\ge0,\ \eta(p,p)\le0\}$. The local orbit result below proves that $p\mapsto\chi_p$ is the full dual-coordinate homeomorphism. Under this convention $\chi_p(te_0)=e^{-itp^0}$.

Assume AC. If $U:G\to U(\mathcal H)$ is a strongly continuous unitary representation as in [[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]], the restriction $a\mapsto U(a,e)$ has its unique regular projection-valued spectral measure $P_U$ on $\widehat{\mathbb R^D}$ supplied by [[lem-spectral-measure-of-a-representation-of-an-abelian-lch-group]]. The representation is **positive-energy** when
$$
P_U(\widehat C_+)=I_{\mathcal H}.
$$
Equivalently, after the orbit lemma identifies $\widehat{\mathbb R^D}$ with momentum space, $P_U$ is concentrated on the closed future cone $C_+=\{p:p^0\ge0,\ \eta(p,p)\le0\}$ and the spectral coordinate $p^0$ is the nonnegative generator $P^0$ in $U(te_0,e)=e^{-itP^0}$. A unitary representation is **irreducible** and **strongly continuous** with the meanings in [[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]].
lem-mackey-induction-classification-for-:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$, let $K$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff group acting continuously by linear automorphisms on $N=\mathbb R^d$, and put $G=N\rtimes K$ with the product topology and the multiplication of [[def-external-semidirect-product]]. Let $\widehat N$ be the Pontryagin dual with $k\cdot\chi=\chi\circ\alpha_{k^{-1}}$. Suppose the dual $K$-action on all of $\widehat N$ has a countable family of invariant Borel sets separating distinct orbits. For each orbit $O$ fix $\chi_O\in O$, let $K_{\chi_O}=\{k\in K:k\cdot\chi_O=\chi_O\}$, and set $H_{\chi_O}=N\rtimes K_{\chi_O}$. Then
$$
(O,[\theta])\longmapsto\left[\operatorname{Ind}_{H_{\chi_O}}^G(\chi_O\otimes\theta)\right]
$$
is a bijection from pairs consisting of a $K$-orbit and a unitary-equivalence class of irreducible strongly continuous unitary representations $\theta$ of $K_{\chi_O}$ to the equivalence classes of irreducible strongly continuous unitary representations of $G$. Here
$$
(\chi_O\otimes\theta)(a,h)=\chi_O(a)\theta(h)\qquad(a\in N,\ h\in K_{\chi_O}).
$$
Changing the orbit representative conjugates the stabilizer and its representation. Different orbits give inequivalent induced representations. In the induced model the translation spectral PVM is multiplication over $X=G/H_\chi$, transported Borelly to $O$ with the full-support quasi-invariant measure from induction; it is concentrated on the inducing orbit $O$.
lem-lorentz-stabilizers-and-connected-co:
## Statement

Let $D\ge2$, $L=SO_0(D-1,1)$, and $c:K\to L$ be a connected covering homomorphism as in [[def-connected-poincare-cover-and-positive-energy]]. For $p_m=me_0$ with $m>0$, the stabilizer in $L$ is $SO(D-1)$. For a fixed future null $p_+$, choose a null frame $e_+,e_-,\mathbb R^n$ with $n=D-2$, $\eta(e_+,e_-)=-1$, and $\eta|_{\mathbb R^n}$ Euclidean. Its stabilizer is
$$
L_{p_+}\cong\mathbb R^n\rtimes SO(n),
$$
where $SO(0)$ is trivial. At zero the stabilizer is all of $L$. Every $L_p$ is closed, and the stabilizer in $K$ is the full inverse image $K_p=c^{-1}(L_p)$. Since $c$ is onto, $K$ and $L$ have the same orbits on momentum space.

The connected covers and the relevant preimages are as follows.

- If $D=2$, $L\cong\mathbb R$ has no nontrivial connected cover. The massive and nonzero null stabilizers are trivial; the zero stabilizer is $K=L$.
- If $D=3$, write $z$ for the deck element in the universal cover $\widetilde L$ corresponding to a positive $2\pi$ spatial rotation. All connected covers are $K_N=\widetilde L/\langle z^N\rangle$ for $N=1,2,\ldots$, and $K_\infty=\widetilde L$. The massive preimage is $\mathbb R/(2\pi N\mathbb Z)$ for finite $N$ and $\mathbb R$ for $N=\infty$. The null preimage is $\mathbb R\times(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)$ for finite $N$ and $\mathbb R\times\mathbb Z$ for $N=\infty$. The zero preimage is $K_N$ itself.
- If $D\ge4$, the only connected covers are $L$ and its universal double cover $\widetilde L$. The massive preimages are respectively $SO(D-1)$ and $\mathrm{Spin}(D-1)$. Put $n=D-2$. The null preimages are respectively $\mathbb R^n\rtimes SO(n)$ and $\mathbb R^n\rtimes\mathrm{Spin}(n)$, where $\mathrm{Spin}(r)$ for $r\ge3$ denotes the universal cover of $SO(r)$. When $D=4$, $\mathrm{Spin}(2)$ means the connected double cover $\mathbb R/(4\pi\mathbb Z)\to SO(2)$, not the universal cover $\mathbb R$. The zero preimage is all of $K$.

Every such $K$ is second-countable locally compact Hausdorff.
For the standard inclusions $SO(r-1)\hookrightarrow SO(r)$, the induced map on $\pi_1$ is an isomorphism for $r\ge4$ and is surjective for $r=3$.
For every $r\ge3$, $\mathrm{Spin}(r)\to SO(r)$ is a two-sheeted universal cover; $\mathrm{Spin}(2)=\mathbb R/(4\pi\mathbb Z)$ is the connected double cover of $SO(2)$ used above.
lem-null-little-group-unitary-duals-for-:
## Statement

Let $D\ge2$, let $K\to SO_0(D-1,1)$ be a connected cover, and let $p$ be a nonzero future null momentum. Write $K_p$ for its full stabilizer preimage. The unitary-equivalence classes of irreducible strongly continuous unitary representations of $K_p$ are as follows.

- If $D\ge4$, put $n=D-2$. By [[lem-lorentz-stabilizers-and-connected-cover-preimages]], $K_p=\mathbb R^n\rtimes C$, where $C=SO(n)$ for the base Lorentz group and $C=\mathrm{Spin}(n)$ for its universal double cover; for $n=2$, $\mathrm{Spin}(2)=\mathbb R/(4\pi\mathbb Z)$. Let $\widehat{\mathbb R^n}$ be identified with $\mathbb R^n$ by its Euclidean characters $\chi_\xi(v)=e^{i\xi\cdot v}$. The $C$-orbits are $\{0\}$ and the spheres $|\xi|=\rho>0$. Over $0$ the little-group representations are all irreducible strongly continuous unitary representations of $C$. Over $\rho>0$, choose $\xi=\rho e_1$ and let $C_\xi$ be its stabilizer. For $C=SO(n)$, $C_\xi=SO(n-1)$ (with $SO(1)=\{1\}$); for $C=\mathrm{Spin}(n)$, $C_\xi$ is the full inverse image of $SO(n-1)$, namely $\mathrm{Spin}(n-1)$ for $n\ge3$, and $\{\pm1\}$ for $n=2$. The representations over this sphere are exactly
  $$\operatorname{Ind}_{\mathbb R^n\rtimes C_\xi}^{\mathbb R^n\rtimes C}(\chi_\xi\otimes\tau),$$
  with $\tau$ any irreducible strongly continuous unitary representation of $C_\xi$; at the fixed representative $\xi$, equivalence is exactly equivalence of $\tau$. In particular, the base $D=4$ group has one representation for each $\rho>0$, while the double-cover group has two, corresponding to the two characters of $\{\pm1\}$. Every $\rho>0$ induced Hilbert space is infinite-dimensional.
In each $\rho>0$ model, a little translation $v\in\mathbb R^n$ acts over $\eta\in S_\rho$ by the multiplier $e^{i\eta\cdot v}$, so the little translations act nontrivially.
- If $D=3$, for $K_N=\widetilde L/\langle z^N\rangle$ the null stabilizer is $\mathbb R\times(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)$; for $K_\infty=\widetilde L$ it is $\mathbb R\times\mathbb Z$. Every irreducible representation is the character
  $$\theta_{t,\alpha}(u,j)=e^{itu}e^{2\pi i\alpha j},\qquad t\in\mathbb R.$$
  For finite $N$, $\alpha\in\frac1N\mathbb Z/\mathbb Z$; for $N=\infty$, $\alpha\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$. Thus $t>0$ and $t<0$ give inequivalent nontrivial null-translation characters, no rotation identifies the signs, and the central phase is an independent parameter. These little-group spaces are one-dimensional.
- If $D=2$, the two nonzero future null rays have trivial stabilizer and hence have the single trivial little-group representation each.

Here induced representations and their equivalences are those of [[lem-mackey-induction-classification-for-regular-euclidean-duals]]. The $D\ge4$ statement concerns the full inverse-image group for each of the two connected Lorentz covers, not just its Lie algebra.
lem-central-kernel-descent-for-poincare-:
## Statement

Let $c:K\to L=SO_0(D-1,1)$ be a connected Lorentz cover, $G=\mathbb R^D\rtimes K$ the connected-cover Poincaré group, and $\Gamma\le\ker c$. Put $\bar K=K/\Gamma$ and $\bar G=\mathbb R^D\rtimes\bar K$. Let $p\in\mathbb R^D$ and let $\theta$ be an irreducible strongly continuous unitary representation of $K_p=c^{-1}(L_p)$. Then
$$
\pi_{p,\theta}=\operatorname{Ind}_{\mathbb R^D\rtimes K_p}^{G}(\chi_p\otimes\theta)
$$
factors through $G\to\bar G$ if and only if $\theta(\gamma)=I$ for every $\gamma\in\Gamma$. Each such $\theta(\gamma)$ is scalar. This criterion applies separately to massive, null, and zero momentum; it does not assert extension to disconnected groups containing parity or time reversal.

In $D\ge4$, for the universal double cover and its nontrivial deck element $z$, $\theta(z)=\pm I$, and descent to the base Lorentz group is exactly the $+I$ case. In $D=3$, let $K_\infty=\widetilde L$ and $K_N=\widetilde L/\langle z^N\rangle$. On the massive little group $\mathbb R$, write $\theta_s(r)=e^{isr}$, $s\in\mathbb R$; it descends from $K_\infty$ to $K_N$ exactly when $Ns\in\mathbb Z$. On the null little group $\mathbb R\times\mathbb Z$, write $\theta_{t,\alpha}(u,j)=e^{itu}e^{2\pi i\alpha j}$; it descends exactly when $N\alpha\in\mathbb Z$, independently of $t$. On the zero orbit, descent of an arbitrary irreducible $K_\infty$ representation $\sigma$ is exactly $\sigma(z^N)=I$.
thm-positive-energy-wigner-mackey-classi:
## Statement

Fix $D\ge2$, a connected Lorentz cover $c:K\to L=SO_0(D-1,1)$, and $G=\mathbb R^D\rtimes K$ with the conventions of [[def-connected-poincare-cover-and-positive-energy]]. Assume AC. Let
$$
C_+=\{p\in\mathbb R^D:p^0\ge0,\ \eta(p,p)\le0\}.
$$
The equivalence classes of irreducible strongly continuous positive-energy unitary representations of $G$ are exactly
$\pi_{p,\theta}=\operatorname{Ind}_{\mathbb R^D\rtimes K_p}^{G}(\chi_p\otimes\theta),\qquad p\in C_+.$
where $K_p=c^{-1}(L_p)$ and $\theta$ runs over the equivalence classes of irreducible strongly continuous unitary representations of $K_p$. Two labels $(p,\theta)$ and $(q,\theta')$ give equivalent representations exactly when $q=k\cdot p$ for some $k\in K$ and $\theta'$ is equivalent to the conjugate representation of $K_q=kK_pk^{-1}$. In particular, zero momentum has the full Lorentz-cover little group $K_0=K$; it is not restricted to the trivial representation.

The stabilizers and their covers are those of [[lem-lorentz-stabilizers-and-connected-cover-preimages]]. For $p$ future timelike, use $p_m=me_0$ with $m=\sqrt{-\eta(p,p)}>0$: $K_{p_m}$ is trivial for $D=2$, is $\mathbb R/(2\pi N\mathbb Z)$ or $\mathbb R$ for the $D=3$ cover $K_N$ or $K_\infty$, and is $SO(D-1)$ or $\mathrm{Spin}(D-1)$ for $D\ge4$. For nonzero future null $p$, the $D\ge4$ little groups and their complete unitary duals are given in [[lem-null-little-group-unitary-duals-for-all-dimensions]]; for $D=3$ they include both signs of the real null-translation character and the independent central phase; for $D=2$ the two future null rays are distinct and each has trivial stabilizer. A representation induced from $p$ also descends through any quotient of its Lorentz cover by $\Gamma\le\ker c$ exactly when $\theta(\gamma)=I$ for every $\gamma\in\Gamma$, as in [[lem-central-kernel-descent-for-poincare-inductions]].

No conclusion about parity, time reversal, spin-statistics, or quantum-field-theoretic particle interpretation is part of this classification.
